notes.title: The Rise of the Golden Idol - DLC and Detective Pass FAQ
notes.notes:
[p]Ahead of our first DLC releasing, we wanted to ensure you have the information you need about how the Detective Pass works and what's included. 
 
[b]Q: How does the Detective Pass work?[/b]
A: If you purchase the Detective Pass, you will get the four [i]The Rise of the Golden Idol[/i] DLCs when they come out at a discounted price to buying them separately. Buying the Detective Pass is less expensive than buying the four DLCs individually.  [/p][p][/p][p] [b]Q: Will I get the DLC straight away if I buy the Detective Pass?[/b]
A: Yes, if you purchase the Detective Pass each DLC will be available for you to download straight away when it releases. 

[b]Q: What is included in the Detective Pass?[/b]
A: All four DLC are included, at a discounted price than if you bought them individually. Only the Steam version of the Detective Pass includes the soundtrack, this is not included on console.

[b]Q: Can I buy the DLC now and the Detective Pass later?[/b]
A: If you buy a DLC now, and decide later to get the Detective Pass, the discount will not be applied - you will have paid the full (or sale) price for the DLC, and then the price of the Detective Pass.

[b]Q: What platforms can I buy the Detective Pass on?[/b] A: You can buy the Detective Pass on PC, PlayStation, Xbox and Nintendo. [/p][p][/p][p]  [b]Q: Do I only need the Detective Pass to play the DLC?[/b] A: No, you would need to own [i]The Rise of the Golden Idol[/i] base game. The DLC will not work if you only own [i]The Case of the Golden Idol[/i].  [/p][p][/p][p][b]Q: How many cases are there in The Sins of New Wells DLC?[/b] A: There are four new cases to explore and solve in [i]The Sins of New Wells[/i] DLC.  [/p][p][/p][p] [b]Q: Will the soundtrack included in the Steam version of the Detective Pass be updated to include DLC tracks?[/b] A: Yes, the intention is to update the soundtrack with DLC tracks! [/p][p][/p][p][b] Q: How many cases does The Lemurian Phoenix have?[/b] A: There are five new cases to solve in The Lemurian Phoenix [/p][p][/p][p][b]Q: How many cases does The Age of Restraint have? [/b]A: There are four new cases to solve in The Age of Restraint[/p][p][/p][p] If you have any more questions, please pop them in the comments below. Make sure to take a look at our [url="https://twitter.com/ColorGray7"]Twitter/X[/url] and [url="https://bsky.app/profile/goldenidol.bsky.social"]Bluesky[/url] for some...interesting...posts.[/p][p][/p][p][/p]

[list]
[*]Numerous text tweaks in all 12 languages, thanks to your feedback.

notes.title: The Rise of the Golden Idol available now!
notes.notes:
Hello Detectives,

We’re thrilled that The Rise of the Golden Idol has now launched! Out on PC, Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch, this sequel builds on the world we introduced in The Case of the Golden Idol and draws us ever deeper into the mystery of the eponymous relic. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2716400/The_Rise_of_the_Golden_Idol/

But why a sequel? What more is there to tell? Let’s unravel the development of The Rise of the Golden Idol together…

[h2]The Idol rises again [/h2]
There is so much more of the story of the Golden Idol to explore. We wanted to see where we could take the story and how the Idol’s power might be influential with a whole new cast of characters and in a very different setting.

Against the backdrop of growing enlightenment and cult panic, The Rise of the Golden Idol takes place 200 years after the unspeakable fate of the Cloudsleys in The Case of the Golden Idol. Now in the 1970s, the legend of the Idol has all but faded into the annals of history and myth, as global political tensions and societal unrest dominate headlines. 

In a period of great change, one thing remains constant: the desire to utilize such a powerful artifact to reshape the world. We wanted to explore how a more modern world - with phones and television - might influence a person’s use of the Idol - and how the Idol might influence that new setting. 

With 20 new cases to untangle, brand new players will be able to step into Rise without having played the first instalment, while players of the first game will definitely be able to pick up some subtle references. Whether you’re a veteran detective or a newly minted investigator, you’ll find yourself immersed in the world of the Golden Idol.

[h2]A refreshed visual style[/h2]
If you’re familiar with our first game in the series, you will notice that the visual style of The Rise of the Golden Idol is different to that of The Case of the Golden Idol and its DLCs. 

For The Case of the Golden Idol, we focused on pixel art to invoke the adventure game vibes of games of old, a familiar visual language for indie games. For The Rise of the Golden Idol, we decided to focus on exploring a different style more familiar to co-founder Ernests, who has a background as a painter. 

While the visual style of our second game is different, its essence in the characters and environments are still a very recognizable, signature Golden Idol look.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781302/69e2e205003d57d1118c85c3b6ae053dbcd1efe6.jpg[/img]

[h2]New era, New UI[/h2]
One thing we wanted to achieve with The Rise of the Golden Idol was for players to have the ability to explore more complex puzzles and have more freedom in how to solve scenarios. Developing Rise in a new engine gave us the opportunity we were looking for to achieve this: a UI overhaul.

We redesigned the game’s UI and moved from the Exploring - Thinking panels to independent panels where players can track the clues they’ve found, characters they’ve encountered, and fill in the story panel separately. This means we were no longer limited to one screen to create puzzles, allowing us to make them bigger and more varied which was really important to us as game developers.

All these panels can be moved to different areas on the screen, and can be opened - or hidden - at the click of a button. You can have as many or as few open as you’d like during each scenario, and it gives you the freedom to solve scenarios at your own pace and not feel overwhelmed, which we felt the previous UI could do. You can also multitask in your investigation, looking at evidence and a puzzle at the same time. 

For those veteran detectives who felt more at home in the first game’s UI, in the full version of the game there will be a UI scaling setting, so you can make puzzles smaller, fit them all on the screen and then just toggle all of them just like in the first game.

We are aware that for some, there was a specific satisfaction in gathering the clues one by one. Our new streamlined approach with the automated word collection has been implemented to allow players to reduce clicking, and focus more on what the texts say. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781302/43889bc9660397e643daae2590716a9444ea88db.gif[/img]
The new panels mean improved readability and navigation, especially at smaller resolutions. This new UI has already been implemented when we brought The Case of the Golden Idol to Xbox and mobile with Netflix as a result of porting the game to a new engine.


We hope you enjoy diving into the next chapter of the Golden Idol’s story, and join us with each new DLC in 2025: buy The Rise of the Golden Idol - Deluxe Edition and you’ll unlock the Detective Pass, giving you all four DLCs and the game OST. 

~ Andrejs and Ernests Klavins, Color Gray Games

notes.title: Release timing, pricing, and the future of the Golden Idol series
notes.notes:
Hello Detectives,

We have some news to share ahead of the game’s launch next week regarding release timing, pricing, and future plans.

[h3]Release Timing[/h3]
[b][i]The Rise of the Golden Idol[/i] will be releasing worldwide on all platforms November 12, 2024 @10AM PST.[/b]

The Nintendo Switch release has been hit with an unexpected delay in a few territories and will now be releasing on November 14, 2024 @ 10AM PST.

[h3]Pricing & Looking Forward[/h3]
[b][i]The Rise of the Golden Idol[/i] will be launching at $19.99 or Steam's regional recommended equivalent. For the first week we will also be offering a 10% launch discount[/b], so take advantage of that before it is gone.

[b]Additionally - today we are announcing that we will be continuing to support[i] The Rise of the Golden Idol[/i] throughout 2025 with new content.[/b] There are a ton of additional standalone stories we want to tell set in the Golden Idol universe, and we found that the best way to tell these stories is through four self-contained DLC chapters - called Investigations.

Similar to the DLC released for [i]The Case of the Golden Idol[/i], these are optional side content and are not required to conclude the story in [i]The Rise of the Golden Idol[/i]. Rather, these are for fans who want more puzzles, more characters, and more mysteries to solve. Each of the four Investigations chapters will include at least four new cases to solve. On top of the base game’s 20 scenarios - that is a lot of sleuthing.

Our roadmap has a sneak peak at the first Investigations chapter and when you can expect all future content to drop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781302/289379ee65a83e1a5be7b5332dca277155c63093.png[/img]

These will be available for sale individually as they release for $5.99 or as part of the [i]Detective's Pass[/i], a discounted pack of all four chapters and the complete soundtrack for $17.99. [b]We will also be offering a permanent stacking discount for owners of [i]The Case of the Golden Idol[/i], so that you can pick up [i]The Rise of the Golden Idol[/i] and all future content at an even cheaper price.[/b]

We can’t wait for you all to dive into the next installment of Golden Idol when it launches next week.

- Team Idol

notes.title: Release Date Reveal, Extended Demo, and Case Redux
notes.notes:
Hello Detectives,

We have lots of exciting news to share for new and returning fans of Golden Idol.

[h2]Release Date - November 12, 2024[/h2]
The Rise of the Golden Idol will be launching on Steam, Nintendo Switch, Xbox Series, PlayStation 5, and Mobile approximately one month from now. Check out the new release date trailer for a sneak peek at what’s in store.

[previewyoutube=BlOOlkAc4N4;full][/previewyoutube]


[h2]Steam Next Fest Demo - Available now![/h2]

We have prepared an extended demo including all the content from the previous demo as well as an additional case for players to solve. While officially the demo is part of the upcoming Steam Next Fest, eager detectives can get their hands on it starting today.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2716400/The_Rise_of_the_Golden_Idol/


[h2]The Case of the Golden Idol Redux Update - Available now![/h2]

Last week we announced a new update coming to The Case of the Golden Idol - called Redux. Learn more about that announcement here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1677770/view/4677641741933164088

The update is available today for all current (and future) owners of The Case of the Golden Idol. You should be prompted to update the next time you launch the game, and choose either the classic or Redux version to launch. While this update features no new playable cases or scenarios, it introduces a number of new features that make it a smoother experience overall.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1677770/The_Case_of_the_Golden_Idol/

Here are some highlights from the Redux update.

[h3]12 supported languages:[/h3]
English (US)
French
Italian 
German
Spanish (Latin America)
Spanish (Spain)
Portuguese (Brazil)
Japanese
Korean 
Polish
Turkish
Chinese (Traditional)

*Chinese (Simplified) will be made available at a later date. 

[h3]New UI & Hint System[/h3]
Returning players should notice an overhaul to the UI, which should improve readability and navigation, especially at smaller resolutions. Additionally, there are now markers that indicate what objects can be interacted with, so no more guessing or using guides when you get stuck.


[h3]Steam Deck Support[/h3]
Support for Steam Deck is now in beta. In addition to running smoother, the UI and text should now scale to appropriately fit the screen size. Once the review process completes, The Case of the Golden Idol will be listed as a Verified title on the store and in your library, a process we expect to take a few weeks.

[b]For Nintendo Switch Owners[/b] - The new release of The Case of the Golden Idol: Complete Edition will need to be manually claimed on the Nintendo eShop, and is free for all current owners. This rerelease includes all of the above changes and addresses an infrequent issue that caused some players to lose all save progress.

[h3]And finally…[/h3]
A thanks from Team Idol & Playstack for all the support for the Golden Idol over the past couple years. We hope you enjoy the demo and can’t wait for everyone to check out The Rise of the Golden Idol when it releases next month.

Wishlist, follow, tell a friend, etc.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2716400/The_Rise_of_the_Golden_Idol/

- Team Idol

notes.title: 2022's best murder mystery game returns with a '70s twist
notes.notes:
Unraveling a good mystery brings a satisfaction like almost no other, whether it be in a more explicit format like Return of the Obra Dinn, Disco Elysium, or Danganronpa, or a more roundabout manner such as Outer Wilds or What Remains of Edith Finch. The Case of the Golden Idol is one of the most successful examples of top-notch murder mystery adventure games in recent memory, earning itself a very worthy 98% Steam rating. As developer Color Gray Games announces its '70s sequel, you can grab the excellent first game at a big discount.
